## 1. Problem Summary

### Background

ClearAuth's exception-tier appeal runs park at the `hold` node via
`interrupt()` and surface in `GET /api/reviews/pending` — a tenant-scoped
queue listing runs that have a `done` audit record, no `human_edited` record,
and a live LangGraph checkpoint (ADR-0011). Since S3 Slice 4b the resume
endpoint (`POST /api/appeal/resume`) is live and the `reviewed_by` field on
the `AuditRecord` is stamped from the session's `user_id` (ADR-0013).

However, the queue today is a **pool, not a workqueue**: any authenticated
reviewer in a tenant can call resume on any parked run. There is no mechanism
to:

- **Assign** a parked case to a named reviewer, preventing duplicate work and
  establishing clear accountability.
- **Notify** the assigned reviewer that a case is waiting, or alert a
  supervisor when an SLA threshold is approaching.
- **Track** who claimed a case and when, separate from who ultimately submitted
  the resume.

### The Gap (G4)

Gap G4 — *Assignment & Notifications* — was identified during the 2026-07-17
platform review as a pre-requisite to the Operate role's production readiness.
Without assignment and notifications the `ready_for_review` and `exception`
queues can only be worked by reviewers who proactively poll the UI, and a case
can be silently double-claimed or abandoned at handoff. Regulatory turnaround
clocks (state-level prior-authorization statutes: Illinois SB 1451, MD HB
1563) make silent abandonment a compliance risk.

### Current State Inventory

| Capability | Status |
|---|---|
| Exception-tier park + resume (`hold` node, ADR-0010) | Live |
| `GET /api/reviews/pending` — tenant-scoped queue (ADR-0011) | Live |
| `reviewed_by` stamped on resume `AuditRecord` (ADR-0013) | Live |
| Tenancy fields on all case-bearing objects (ADR-0017) | Live |
| `TenancyScope` fail-closed at store boundary | Live |
| Assignment of a case to a named reviewer | **Missing** |
| Claim / unclaim lifecycle on the queue item | **Missing** |
| In-app notification delivery | **Missing** |
| SLA / urgency-driven notification escalation | **Missing** |
| Supervisor override (re-assign a claimed case) | **Missing** |

---

## 2. Goals

**G4-01.** A reviewer (Operate role) can claim a pending case from the
exception queue, producing a durable `AssignmentRecord` that links the
`correlation_id` of the parked run to a `user_id` and a `tenant_id`.

**G4-02.** Once claimed, the case is **locked** to that reviewer: attempts by
a second reviewer to claim the same `correlation_id` return a typed conflict
response rather than silently racing.

**G4-03.** The assigned reviewer can release a claim (unclaim), returning the
case to the pool — with an audit entry.

**G4-04.** A supervisor (a user with the `supervisor` role claim — see
ADR-0017 Q4's deferred `role` field, which G4 adds) can forcibly re-assign a
claimed case to another reviewer.

**G4-05.** The notification system delivers an in-app notification to the
assigned reviewer when a case is claimed against them (supervisor-assign path)
or when a new exception-tier run parks in their tenant (pool notification).

**G4-06.** SLA-age notifications fire when a parked run has been in the queue
past configurable thresholds (default: **2 h** first reminder, **4 h**
escalation to supervisor).

**G4-07.** Notifications are tenant-scoped, delivered over the existing SSE
transport extended with a persistent `notification` event, and retrievable via
a new `GET /api/notifications` endpoint.

**G4-08.** All assignment and notification state is stored in the pre-Phase-3
in-memory stores (same caveat as the audit list and session store; PostgreSQL
migration lands at Phase 3 with the rest of the durable store).

**G4-09.** The LangGraph pipeline emits an `AssignmentHook` after the `hold`
interrupt fires, allowing the notification subsystem to send the initial
"case parked" tenant notification without coupling the pipeline to HTTP or a
message broker.

**G4-10.** The change is **behavior-preserving** for the existing resume path:
`POST /api/appeal/resume` continues to work as-is; the assignment layer is
additive, not a gate on resume for this slice (enforcement gate deferred to G4
Slice 2).

---

## 3. Non-Goals

- **Email or SMS notifications.** Only in-app SSE delivery is in scope. Push
  email is a distinct integration (outbound dispatch rail, gap G7).
- **Role-based access control enforcement on resume.** The assignment record
  establishes attribution this slice; blocking unclaimed resumes is deferred.
- **Notification delivery guarantees (at-least-once / exactly-once).** The
  in-memory store is best-effort pre-Phase-3; notifications that arrive before
  a client connects are readable via the REST endpoint but not re-pushed.
- **SLA clock integration with regulatory deadlines.** Thresholds are
  operator-configured flat durations; real regulatory-deadline logic (drug ×
  payer × state) is a later roadmap item.
- **Assignment of `routine` or `complex` tier cases.** Those tiers do not park
  at `hold` and are not in the exception queue; queue workspace assignment is a
  separate track.
- **Multi-tenant admin panel.** Platform-plane (Bearer) visibility of
  cross-tenant assignments is read-only this slice.
- **Qdrant or PostgreSQL.** No new external dependencies introduced; stores
  remain in-process.
- **`demo` branch changes.** The assignment/notification surfaces ship only in
  `main`; the demo SPA continues to run from fixtures.

---

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| FR-01 | `POST /api/cases/{correlation_id}/assign` — claim or assign a parked case; body specifies optional `assignee_id` (supervisor path) or defaults to the session user. |
| FR-02 | A second claim on an already-assigned `correlation_id` returns `409 Conflict` with the current `AssignmentRecord` in the body. |
| FR-03 | `DELETE /api/cases/{correlation_id}/assign` — release (unclaim) a case; only the current assignee or a supervisor may unclaim. |
| FR-04 | `PATCH /api/cases/{correlation_id}/assign` — re-assign (supervisor only); atomically replaces `assignee_id` and writes a new `AssignmentEvent`. |
| FR-05 | `GET /api/reviews/pending` response is extended (additive, non-breaking) with an optional `assignee_id: str \| null` field per review item. |
| FR-06 | `GET /api/notifications` returns the authenticated user's (tenant-scoped) notification list, ordered newest-first, with read/unread state. |
| FR-07 | `POST /api/notifications/{notification_id}/read` marks a single notification read. |
| FR-08 | `POST /api/notifications/read-all` marks all of the user's notifications read. |
| FR-09 | The SSE stream for `GET /api/reviews/stream` (new; see §8) pushes `notification` events to connected clients in real time. |
| FR-10 | When an exception-tier run parks (`hold` node fires), a tenant-wide `case_parked` notification is created for all Operate-role users in the tenant within 500 ms. |
| FR-11 | When a supervisor assigns a case to a specific reviewer, a `case_assigned` notification targets that reviewer's `user_id`. |
| FR-12 | SLA-age notifications fire at configurable intervals; defaults are 2 h (`sla_reminder`) and 4 h (`sla_escalation`), the latter targeting supervisors. |
| FR-13 | Notification records carry `correlation_id`, `tenant_id`, `target_user_id` (or `null` = tenant-wide), `notification_type`, `created_at`, `read_at`, and a short `message` string (no PHI — identifiers only, per ADR-0009 §side-channel rules). |
| FR-14 | The `AssignmentRecord` carries `correlation_id`, `tenant_id`, `assignee_id`, `assigned_by`, `assigned_at`, `released_at \| null`. |
| FR-15 | `AuditRecord` gains an `assignment_ref: str \| null` field stamped with the `assignee_id` at resume time when a claim exists, so the audit trail closes the claim→review→submit loop. |
| FR-16 | All new read paths are fail-closed through `TenancyScope` — no scope, no rows (same invariant as §7 of 07-security-architecture.md). |
| FR-17 | A Bearer/platform caller sees all tenants' assignment and notification records (platform-plane read, consistent with ADR-0017). |

### 4.2 Non-Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Claim/unclaim/re-assign operations are idempotent within a `(correlation_id, attempt)` window — a duplicate claim by the same `user_id` within 30 s returns `200` with the existing record (not `409`). |
| NFR-02 | In-memory assignment store must be read-consistent within the same Python process (single-worker pre-Phase-3, matching the audit and session store caveats in ADR-0009). |
| NFR-03 | The SSE notification stream (`GET /api/reviews/stream`) must not block appeal generation — it runs on a separate route with its own async generator and does not share state with the pipeline SSE routes. |
| NFR-04 | SLA-age checks are driven by a lightweight `asyncio` background task started at `main.py` startup — no Celery, no external scheduler (deferred dep rule, ADR-0007). |
| NFR-05 | No PHI in any notification message field — only `correlation_id`, `scenario_id`, `drug` (drug name is not PHI), `plan`, and `tier`. |
| NFR-06 | All new Pydantic models follow the strict-mode pattern (`ConfigDict(strict=True)`) established in `models/schemas.py`. |
| NFR-07 | Frontend/backend parity: new enums and shared shapes are mirrored in `src/types.ts` in the same commit; parity enforced by `test_schema_parity.py` (existing gate). |
| NFR-08 | New routes are covered by at least one integration test in `tests/integration/` before the PR merges (TDD — RED before GREEN). |
| NFR-09 | SLA thresholds are configurable via environment variables (`SLA_REMINDER_HOURS`, `SLA_ESCALATION_HOURS`) with the defaults above; no hard-coded magic numbers in production code. |

---

## 5. Assignment Model

### 5.1 Conceptual Design

The assignment model is a **thin claim layer over the existing queue index**
(ADR-0011). It does not replace or duplicate the audit-trail-derived queue; it
adds a mutable `AssignmentRecord` keyed by `correlation_id` that the queue
read path joins into its response.

```
pending review queue (audit-derived, immutable)
        │
        │  joined at read time
        ▼
AssignmentRecord (mutable, keyed by correlation_id)
        │
        │  stamped at resume time
        ▼
AuditRecord (human_edited, assignment_ref field)
```

### 5.2 Claim Lifecycle

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> unassigned : exception run parks (hold node)
    unassigned --> assigned : POST /assign (self-claim or supervisor-assign)
    assigned --> unassigned : DELETE /assign (release by assignee or supervisor)
    assigned --> assigned : PATCH /assign (supervisor re-assign — replaces assignee_id)
    assigned --> resolved : POST /api/appeal/resume succeeds → human_edited AuditRecord written
    unassigned --> resolved : resume by any reviewer (no claim — assignment_ref = null)
    resolved --> [*]
```

### 5.3 Claim Conflict Semantics

A `correlation_id` maps to **at most one live `AssignmentRecord`**. The store
enforces this with a compare-and-swap write — if a record already exists for
the `correlation_id` and its `released_at` is `null`, the write is rejected and
the store returns the existing record. The route translates this into `409`.

Idempotent window (NFR-01): the same `(correlation_id, user_id)` pair within
30 s is treated as a transport retry and returns `200` with the existing record.
This mirrors the audit idempotency semantics (ADR-0009) without re-inventing
the `idempotency_key` scheme for a mutable entity.

### 5.4 Role Model (Additive to ADR-0017)

ADR-0017 deferred the `role` claim on the session to Phase 3. G4 needs it
for the supervisor path. This slice adds a minimal `UserRole` enum and a
`role` field to `LoginResponse` / `MeResponse` without a full RBAC overhaul:

| Role | Capabilities added by G4 |
|---|---|
| `reviewer` | Self-claim, unclaim own cases, resume any case in tenant |
| `supervisor` | All reviewer capabilities + assign to others, force re-assign, receive `sla_escalation` notifications |
| `service` | Bearer callers — platform-plane read, no assignment operations |

The pre-DB implementation seeds `DEMO_USER` as `reviewer` and a new
`DEMO_SUPERVISOR_USER` / `DEMO_SUPERVISOR_PASSWORD` as `supervisor`. A future
ADR covers role persistence in PostgreSQL.

### 5.5 Integration with Resume

`POST /api/appeal/resume` is unchanged in signature. The route handler gains
one additive step:

```
1. auth_middleware resolves session user_id (existing)
2. look up AssignmentRecord for correlation_id (new — assignment_store.get())
3. if record exists → stamp assignment_ref = record.assignee_id on the
   AuditRecord written by run_resume (new field, null if no claim)
4. mark record released_at = now (new — assignment_store.release())
5. run_resume() as before (unchanged)
```

This is **not** a blocking gate — an unclaimed resume succeeds with
`assignment_ref = null`. The blocking gate (only the assignee may resume) is
deferred to G4 Slice 2.

---

## 6. Notification System

### 6.1 Architecture

The notification system is a **lightweight in-process pub/sub** with three
components:

1. **`NotificationStore`** (`backend/notifications/store.py`) — in-memory
   `dict[str, list[NotificationRecord]]` keyed by `tenant_id`; a secondary
   index by `target_user_id`; bounded to 1000 records per tenant (LRU eviction
   on oldest-read). Thread-safe via `asyncio.Lock` (single-event-loop
   assumption, pre-Phase-3).

2. **`NotificationBus`** (`backend/notifications/bus.py`) — an
   `asyncio.Queue`-backed fan-out. Publishers push `NotificationRecord` objects
   in; active SSE streams (one per connected client) drain from a per-client
   sub-queue. The bus is a module-level singleton (same pattern as the compiled
   `_PIPELINE` in `agents/graph.py`).

3. **SLA ticker** (`backend/notifications/sla_ticker.py`) — an `asyncio`
   background task (started in `main.py`'s `lifespan` handler) that wakes
   every 5 minutes, scans the pending-review queue, and emits `sla_reminder` /
   `sla_escalation` events for runs older than the configured thresholds.

### 6.2 Notification Types

| `notification_type` | Trigger | `target_user_id` |
|---|---|---|
| `case_parked` | Exception-tier `hold` node fires | `null` (tenant-wide) |
| `case_assigned` | Supervisor assigns to a specific reviewer | Assignee's `user_id` |
| `case_released` | Assignee or supervisor unclaims a case | `null` (tenant-wide) |
| `case_reassigned` | Supervisor re-assigns a claimed case | New assignee's `user_id`; old assignee also notified |
| `case_resolved` | `human_edited` `AuditRecord` written | `null` (tenant-wide) |
| `sla_reminder` | Case in queue past `SLA_REMINDER_HOURS` (default 2 h) | Assignee if claimed, else `null` |
| `sla_escalation` | Case in queue past `SLA_ESCALATION_HOURS` (default 4 h) | All supervisors in tenant |

### 6.3 Notification Record Shape

```python
class NotificationRecord(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)

    notification_id: str          # uuid4 hex
    tenant_id: str
    target_user_id: str | None    # None = tenant-wide
    notification_type: NotificationType
    correlation_id: str           # parked run's handle
    scenario_id: str
    drug: str                     # not PHI
    plan: str                     # not PHI
    tier: CaseTier
    message: str                  # ≤ 200 chars; identifiers only, no PHI
    created_at: datetime
    read_at: datetime | None      # None = unread
```

`NotificationType` is a new enum in `backend/models/schemas.py` (mirrored in
`src/types.ts`):

```
case_parked | case_assigned | case_released | case_reassigned
| case_resolved | sla_reminder | sla_escalation
```

### 6.4 SSE Notification Event

The notification event rides the existing SSE wire format
(`event: notification\ndata: <JSON>\n\n`) on the **new** stream route
`GET /api/reviews/stream`. This is intentionally a **separate route** from
`/api/appeal/generate` — the notification stream is long-lived (client keeps
it open) while the generation routes are per-request and terminate. The
existing `AppealEvent` discriminated union is not extended.

```json
{
  "event": "notification",
  "notification_id": "3f7a…",
  "notification_type": "case_parked",
  "correlation_id": "livdelzi-cigna:a1",
  "scenario_id": "livdelzi-cigna",
  "drug": "Livdelzi (seladelpar)",
  "plan": "Cigna PPO",
  "tier": "exception",
  "message": "Exception-tier case livdelzi-cigna:a1 is awaiting review.",
  "created_at": "2026-07-19T14:30:00+00:00"
}
```

A `keepalive` comment frame (`:\n\n`) is sent every 15 s to prevent proxy
timeouts.

### 6.5 Pipeline → Notification Hook (`AssignmentHook`)

The `hold` node in `agents/graph.py` currently calls `interrupt()` and emits
no further events (the SSE stream terminates with the earlier `done` event).
G4 adds a **post-interrupt hook** that publishes to the `NotificationBus` after
`interrupt()` returns:

```python
# agents/nodes/hold.py  (new behaviour in existing node)

async def hold_node(state: PipelineState, config: RunnableConfig) -> PipelineState:
    writer = get_stream_writer()
    await writer({"type": "hold", "correlation_id": state["correlation_id"]})
    # Publish case_parked notification — fire-and-forget, never blocks pipeline
    notification_bus.publish_nowait(
        build_case_parked_notification(state)
    )
    interrupt({"reason": "exception_tier_review"})
    return state
```

`build_case_parked_notification` is a pure function
(`notifications/events.py`) — it constructs a `NotificationRecord` from
`PipelineState` fields without any I/O, consistent with the node-purity rule
(CLAUDE.md §File Organization, doc 02). The bus enqueues without awaiting
delivery, so `interrupt()` is never delayed by notification fan-out.

### 6.6 SLA Ticker Design

```python
# notifications/sla_ticker.py

async def sla_ticker_task(
    review_queue_fn: Callable[[], list[PendingReview]],
    notification_store: NotificationStore,
    notification_bus: NotificationBus,
    *,
    poll_interval_s: int = 300,
    reminder_hours: float,
    escalation_hours: float,
) -> None:
    while True:
        await asyncio.sleep(poll_interval_s)
        now = datetime.now(UTC)
        for review in review_queue_fn():
            age = now - review.parked_at
            if age >= timedelta(hours=escalation_hours):
                _maybe_emit(notification_store, notification_bus, review,
                            NotificationType.sla_escalation)
            elif age >= timedelta(hours=reminder_hours):
                _maybe_emit(notification_store, notification_bus, review,
                            NotificationType.sla_reminder)
```

`_maybe_emit` checks whether a notification of that type for that
`correlation_id` was already emitted in this interval (deduplication via
`NotificationStore.has_recent(correlation_id, notification_type,
within=poll_interval_s)`) — prevents duplicate SLA alerts on each tick.

The ticker is injected with the same `derive_pending_reviews` + `is_run_parked`
pair used by the `/api/reviews/pending` route (ADR-0011), so it shares the
queue index logic without re-implementing it.

---

## 7. Data Model Changes

### 7.1 New Pydantic Models (`backend/models/schemas.py`)

```python
class UserRole(str, Enum):
    reviewer = "reviewer"
    supervisor = "supervisor"
    service = "service"

class NotificationType(str, Enum):
    case_parked     = "case_parked"
    case_assigned   = "case_assigned"
    case_released   = "case_released"
    case_reassigned = "case_reassigned"
    case_resolved   = "case_resolved"
    sla_reminder    = "sla_reminder"
    sla_escalation  = "sla_escalation"

class AssignmentRecord(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
    assignment_id: str             # uuid4 hex
    correlation_id: str
    tenant_id: str
    assignee_id: str               # user_id of the claimed reviewer
    assigned_by: str               # user_id of the actor (self or supervisor)
    assigned_at: datetime
    released_at: datetime | None   # None = still claimed

class AssignmentEvent(BaseModel):
    """Immutable log entry per assignment state transition."""
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
    event_id: str
    correlation_id: str
    tenant_id: str
    event_type: Literal["claimed", "released", "reassigned"]
    actor_id: str
    target_id: str                 # new assignee_id (or "" for release)
    timestamp: datetime

class NotificationRecord(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True)
    notification_id: str
    tenant_id: str
    target_user_id: str | None
    notification_type: NotificationType
    correlation_id: str
    scenario_id: str
    drug: str
    plan: str
    tier: CaseTier
    message: str                   # ≤ 200 chars
    created_at: datetime
    read_at: datetime | None
```

### 7.2 Modifications to Existing Models

**`AuditRecord`** (additive field — no breaking change):
```python
assignment_ref: str | None = None   # assignee_id at resume time; null if unclaimed
```

**`MeResponse`** (additive):
```python
role: UserRole = UserRole.reviewer
```

**`LoginResponse`** (additive):
```python
role: UserRole = UserRole.reviewer
```

**`PendingReview`** (the per-item shape in `PendingReviewsResponse` — additive):
```python
assignee_id: str | None = None      # null if unassigned
assigned_at: datetime | None = None
```

### 7.3 New Enums Added to `src/types.ts` (parity required)

```typescript
export type UserRole = "reviewer" | "supervisor" | "service";

export type NotificationType =
  | "case_parked"
  | "case_assigned"
  | "case_released"
  | "case_reassigned"
  | "case_resolved"
  | "sla_reminder"
  | "sla_escalation";
```

Frontend `LoginResponse` / `MeResponse` types gain the `role: UserRole` field
in the generated `api-types.d.ts` (regenerated by `npm run api:dump &&
npm run api:types`; freshness gate in CI catches any drift — doc 08).

### 7.4 New Store Modules

```
backend/
  notifications/
    __init__.py
    store.py          # NotificationStore — in-memory dict + LRU
    bus.py            # NotificationBus — asyncio.Queue fan-out singleton
    sla_ticker.py     # background task
    events.py         # pure builder functions (no I/O)
  assignment/
    __init__.py
    store.py          # AssignmentStore — compare-and-swap dict
    events.py         # pure AssignmentEvent builders
```

Layer rule: `notifications/` and `assignment/` are new cross-cutting modules
at the same level as `audit/` — they are not inside `agents/`. Route handlers
remain logic-free; all derivation logic lives in these modules (testability,
CLAUDE.md §File Organization).

---

## 8. API Changes

All new routes follow the dual Bearer/cookie auth scheme (ADR-0013) and the
`TenancyScope` fail-closed boundary (ADR-0017). Cookie-authenticated non-GET
requests require `X-CSRF-Token`.

### 8.1 Assignment Routes

#### `POST /api/cases/{correlation_id}/assign`

Claim or assign a parked case.

**Auth:** dual scheme. Cookie writes need CSRF token.

**Path param:** `correlation_id` — must match a parked run in the review queue
(i.e., an exception-tier `done` record + live checkpoint + no `human_edited`
record). If the run is not parked, `404`.

**Request body:**
```json
{ "assignee_id": "user-42" }
```
`assignee_id` is optional — omit to self-claim (defaults to session `user_id`).
Providing `assignee_id != session_user_id` requires the `supervisor` role
(returns `403` otherwise).

**Responses:**

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Claim created or idempotent match — returns `AssignmentRecord` |
| `403` | Insufficient role (reviewer attempting to assign to another user) |
| `404` | `correlation_id` not in the pending queue |
| `409` | Already claimed by a different user — returns existing `AssignmentRecord` in body |
| `422` | Body validation failure |

#### `DELETE /api/cases/{correlation_id}/assign`

Release a claim (unclaim).

**Auth:** dual scheme. The session user must be the current `assignee_id` OR
have the `supervisor` role.

**Responses:** `204` (released), `403` (not assignee and not supervisor),
`404` (no live claim for `correlation_id`).

#### `PATCH /api/cases/{correlation_id}/assign`

Re-assign to a different reviewer (supervisor only).

**Auth:** dual scheme; requires `supervisor` role.

**Request body:**
```json
{ "assignee_id": "user-99" }
```

**Responses:** `200` `AssignmentRecord` (updated), `403` (not supervisor),
`404` (no live claim or `correlation_id` not in queue).

### 8.2 Notification Routes

#### `GET /api/notifications`

Returns the authenticated user's notification list, tenant-scoped.

**Auth:** dual scheme. A Bearer/platform caller sees all tenants (platform-plane).

**Query params:**
- `unread_only: bool` (default `false`)
- `limit: int` (default `50`, max `200`)

**Response:**
```json
{
  "notifications": [
    {
      "notification_id": "3f7a…",
      "notification_type": "case_parked",
      "correlation_id": "livdelzi-cigna:a1",
      "scenario_id": "livdelzi-cigna",
      "drug": "Livdelzi (seladelpar)",
      "plan": "Cigna PPO",
      "tier": "exception",
      "message": "Exception-tier case livdelzi-cigna:a1 is awaiting review.",
      "created_at": "2026-07-19T14:30:00+00:00",
      "read_at": null
    }
  ],
  "unread_count": 1
}
```

#### `POST /api/notifications/{notification_id}/read`

Mark a single notification read.

**Auth:** dual scheme; the session user must own the notification or be a
supervisor in the tenant. `204` on success, `404` if unknown.

#### `POST /api/notifications/read-all`

Mark all of the authenticated user's notifications read.

**Auth:** dual scheme. `204`, no body.

#### `GET /api/reviews/stream`

Long-lived SSE stream delivering `notification` events in real time to the
authenticated client.

**Auth:** dual scheme (Bearer or cookie). Cookie-authenticated — CSRF not
required for GET.

**Response:** `200 text/event-stream`, same headers as the generation routes.
Events:

```
event: notification
data: { ...NotificationRecord fields... }

```

```
:keepalive

```

The client closes the connection to end the stream. On reconnect the client
should call `GET /api/notifications?unread_only=true` to catch any missed
events (not replayed on reconnect — no event-ID replay in this slice;
EventSource retry semantics are a Phase 3 enhancement).

### 8.3 Modified Route Responses

#### `GET /api/reviews/pending` (additive change)

The `reviews` array items gain two optional fields:

```json
{
  "correlation_id": "livdelzi-cigna:a1",
  "scenario_id": "livdelzi-cigna",
  "drug": "Livdelzi (seladelpar)",
  "plan": "Cigna PPO",
  "tier": "exception",
  "parked_at": "2026-07-19T12:00:00+00:00",
  "assignee_id": "user-42",
  "assigned_at": "2026-07-19T12:15:00+00:00"
}
```

`assignee_id` and `assigned_at` are `null` when unassigned. Clients that do
not use these fields are unaffected (additive JSON fields).

#### `GET /api/auth/me` (additive change)

```json
{ "user_id": "reviewer-1", "role": "reviewer" }
```

#### `POST /api/auth/login` (additive change)

```json
{ "user_id": "reviewer-1", "csrf_token": "…", "role": "reviewer" }
```

### 8.4 Environment Variables (New)

| Var | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEMO_SUPERVISOR_USER` | for supervisor login | — | Demo supervisor credentials |
| `DEMO_SUPERVISOR_PASSWORD` | for supervisor login | — | Demo supervisor credentials |
| `SLA_REMINDER_HOURS` | no | `2.0` | Age (hours) triggering `sla_reminder` notification |
| `SLA_ESCALATION_HOURS` | no | `4.0` | Age (hours) triggering `sla_escalation` to supervisors |
| `SLA_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | no | `300` | SLA ticker wake interval |
| `NOTIFICATION_STORE_LIMIT` | no | `1000` | Max notifications per tenant (LRU evict oldest-read) |

## 9. LangGraph Integration

### 9.1 Changes to `agents/graph.py`

The compiled `_PIPELINE` (`StateGraph(PipelineState)`) receives one additive
node-level change: the existing `hold` node wrapper gains a `publish_nowait`
call after `interrupt()`. **The graph topology is unchanged** — no new nodes,
no new edges, no new conditional routing.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> ingestion
    ingestion --> retrieval
    retrieval --> synthesis
    synthesis --> gatekeeper
    gatekeeper --> tier_router : passed
    tier_router --> finalize
    finalize --> done_event
    done_event --> hold : tier == exception
    hold --> [*] : interrupt() + publish_nowait(case_parked) ← NEW
    gatekeeper --> synthesis : failed < 3
    gatekeeper --> error_event : failed == 3
    done_event --> [*] : routine / complex
    error_event --> [*]
```

### 9.2 `PipelineState` changes

One additive field — `correlation_id` already exists (it is the
`thread_id = correlation_id` config value). No `PipelineState` schema change
is needed because `correlation_id` is carried in `config["configurable"]`
and already accessible in all node wrappers.

### 9.3 `hold` node implementation (modified)

```python
# agents/nodes/hold.py  (node wrapper — thin, no business logic)

async def hold_node(state: PipelineState, config: RunnableConfig) -> PipelineState:
    from notifications.bus import notification_bus      # module-level singleton
    from notifications.events import build_case_parked  # pure builder

    writer = get_stream_writer()
    correlation_id: str = config["configurable"]["thread_id"]

    # Publish before interrupt so the notification lands even if interrupt
    # raises (LangGraph interrupt() raises GraphInterrupt internally).
    record = build_case_parked(state, correlation_id=correlation_id)
    notification_bus.publish_nowait(record)   # fire-and-forget

    await writer({"type": "hold", "correlation_id": correlation_id})
    interrupt({"reason": "exception_tier_review"})
    return state
```

`publish_nowait` uses `asyncio.Queue.put_nowait` — it does not block and does
not raise if the queue is full (the bus drops the oldest undelivered event
under backpressure, acceptable for best-effort pre-Phase-3 delivery).

### 9.4 `resume_finalize` node (modified)

The `resume_finalize` node in `agents/resume.py` stamps `assignment_ref` on
the `AuditRecord` it writes. The assignment store is queried via a pure helper:

```python
assignment_ref = assignment_store.get_assignee(correlation_id)
# Returns assignee_id str or None; store.release() called after AuditRecord written
```

After the audit write succeeds, the store's `release` is called to set
`released_at = now`. This order guarantees the audit record lands before the
claim is cleared — matching the "durability before terminal event" invariant
(CLAUDE.md §ACID).

### 9.5 Backward Compatibility

The resume path is contract-stable: `POST /api/appeal/resume` callers see no
change in request shape, SSE event shape, or HTTP status codes. The
`assignment_ref` field on `AuditRecord` is `null` for all runs resumed before
G4 deploys and for unclaimed resumes thereafter.

---

## 10. UI Surfaces

These surfaces ship in the `main` branch only (doc 01 — dual-branch strategy,
ADR-0005). The demo SPA (`demo` branch) continues to render from fixtures.

### 10.1 Pending Review Queue — `src/components/portfolio/ReviewQueue.tsx`

**Current:** renders the list returned by `GET /api/reviews/pending` with
`correlation_id`, drug, plan, tier, and `parked_at`.

**G4 additions (all live-mode only):**

- **Claim button** — for unassigned rows: calls `POST /api/cases/{id}/assign`
  (self-claim). On `409`, shows a tooltip "Assigned to {assignee_id}".
- **Assignee badge** — for assigned rows: shows the `assignee_id` and
  `assigned_at` as a chip. Supervisor sessions show a "Re-assign" action.
- **Release link** — visible to the current assignee: calls
  `DELETE /api/cases/{id}/assign`. Requires confirmation dialog.
- **SLA age indicator** — computes `now − parked_at` client-side; shows amber
  at 2 h, red at 4 h (matches server-side SLA thresholds).

### 10.2 Notification Bell — `src/components/shared/NotificationBell.tsx`

New component added to the Operate-role header bar.

- Unread count badge (integer, capped display at `99+`).
- Click opens a dropdown panel listing the 10 most recent notifications with
  type icon, message, relative timestamp (`parked 12 min ago`), and a link to
  the relevant case in the queue workspace.
- "Mark all read" button calls `POST /api/notifications/read-all`.
- Component mounts `GET /api/reviews/stream` SSE connection on login; incoming
  `notification` events increment the badge and prepend to the dropdown. On
  disconnect it falls back to polling `GET /api/notifications` every 30 s.

### 10.3 Supervisor Assignment Modal — `src/components/portfolio/AssignModal.tsx`

Supervisor-only modal (role-gated: renders only when `me.role === "supervisor"`).

- Triggered from the "Re-assign" queue row action.
- Dropdown of `reviewer`-role users in the tenant (populated from a new
  `GET /api/users` stub — returns the seeded demo users; full user directory
  is Phase 3).
- Submit calls `PATCH /api/cases/{id}/assign`.

### 10.4 Capability Manifest Entry

Following ADR-0016 (single-shell capability manifest), G4 adds two entries to
`src/capabilities.ts`:

```typescript
{
  unit: "O14",
  label: "Case Assignment",
  route: "/queue/assignment",
  live: true,              // live mode: real API
  simulated: false,        // no offline fixture path this slice
  hidden: false,
},
{
  unit: "O15",
  label: "Notifications",
  route: "/notifications",
  live: true,
  simulated: false,
  hidden: false,
},
```

`simulated: false` means the Operate view hides these panels when
`VITE_API_BASE_URL` is unset (offline demo mode). This is intentional — the
demo SPA has no fixture path for assignment state.

## 11. Test Cases

Tests follow the TDD convention (doc 09): RED commit before GREEN commit, named
`test(g4-NNN): RED` / `fix(g4-NNN): GREEN`.

### 11.1 Unit Tests — `backend/tests/unit/`

| Module | Test IDs | What is tested |
|---|---|---|
| `test_assignment_store.py` | G4-U-01 | Claim creates `AssignmentRecord`; idempotent re-claim by same user returns existing record |
| | G4-U-02 | Second claim by different user raises conflict; record returned |
| | G4-U-03 | `release()` sets `released_at`; subsequent claim succeeds |
| | G4-U-04 | `get_assignee()` returns `None` for unknown `correlation_id` |
| `test_notification_store.py` | G4-U-05 | `add()` stores record; `get_for_user()` returns tenant-scoped + target-user-matching records |
| | G4-U-06 | `mark_read()` sets `read_at`; `mark_all_read()` bulk-sets |
| | G4-U-07 | LRU eviction: adding record 1001 evicts oldest-read when limit=1000 |
| | G4-U-08 | `has_recent()` dedup gate: returns `True` if same type + `correlation_id` within interval |
| `test_notification_events.py` | G4-U-09 | `build_case_parked()` constructs correct `NotificationRecord` from `PipelineState`; no PHI in `message` |
| | G4-U-10 | All seven `NotificationType` builders produce well-formed records |
| `test_sla_ticker.py` | G4-U-11 | Ticker emits `sla_reminder` when age ≥ `reminder_hours`; not before |
| | G4-U-12 | Ticker emits `sla_escalation` when age ≥ `escalation_hours`; `sla_reminder` not re-emitted once escalated |
| | G4-U-13 | `has_recent()` dedup prevents duplicate SLA events within one poll interval |
| `test_schema_parity.py` (existing, extended) | G4-U-14 | `UserRole`, `NotificationType` enums exist in both `schemas.py` and `src/types.ts` with identical members |

| File | Test IDs | What is tested |
|---|---|---|
| `test_assignment_api.py` | G4-I-01 | `POST /api/cases/{id}/assign` (self-claim) → `200`; second call same user → `200` idempotent; second call different user → `409` |
| | G4-I-02 | `DELETE /api/cases/{id}/assign` by assignee → `204`; by non-assignee reviewer → `403`; by supervisor → `204` |

## 12. Risks

| ID | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | **Single-worker assumption breaks under multi-worker deploy.** In-memory `AssignmentStore` and `NotificationStore` are not shared across uvicorn workers. | Medium (deploy topology unknown) | High — silent duplicate claims possible | Document the single-worker caveat (mirrors ADR-0009/0010/0011). Add an integration test that asserts the claim conflict is enforced within one process. Migrate to PostgreSQL at Phase 3 with the rest of the durable store. |
| R-02 | **`asyncio.Queue` backpressure drops notifications.** Under burst load (many exception-tier runs parking simultaneously) the bus queue could fill. | Low | Low (best-effort pre-Phase-3) | Set bus queue `maxsize=500`; `put_nowait` silently drops overflow. Log a warning (identifiers only) when drop occurs. Phase 3 migrates to a durable message broker. |
| R-03 | **SLA ticker accumulates unbounded state.** If the SLA store for "already notified" events grows indefinitely it leaks memory. | Medium (long-running process) | Low | Bound the SLA-notified set to 10,000 entries with TTL-based eviction (24 h). |
| R-04 | **Role field on session breaks existing demo login.** Adding `role` to `LoginResponse` / `MeResponse` is additive; existing clients that do not read it are unaffected. | Low | Low | Additive JSON fields; TypeScript consumer upgraded in same PR; parity test catches drift. |
| R-05 | **`hold` node `publish_nowait` after `interrupt()` never executes.** `interrupt()` in LangGraph raises `GraphInterrupt` internally — code after it in the function body does not run. | High if ordered incorrectly | High — no `case_parked` notifications | **Mitigation (required):** call `publish_nowait` **before** `interrupt()`. Confirmed in LangGraph source (ADR-0010 note). Integration test G4-I-11 directly verifies this ordering. |
| R-06 | **Re-assign race between `PATCH` and `DELETE`.** A supervisor re-assigns while the assignee simultaneously unclaims — one operation wins, the other gets `404`. | Low | Low (last-write-wins is acceptable) | Document the behavior. The assignment event log provides a full audit trail for post-hoc reconciliation. |
| R-07 | **`GET /api/reviews/stream` held open by many clients degrades server under load.** SSE streams hold a file descriptor open per client. | Low (demo/early-stage scale) | Medium | Default server: single uvicorn worker with async generator — scales to tens of concurrent SSE connections. Rate-limit SSE connections per session at `slowapi` integration (Phase 3 / hosted backend). |
| R-08 | **Notification messages leak PHI via inadvertent field inclusion.** | Low | High | `build_*` functions are pure and covered by G4-U-09 + PHI scan extension in `test_golden_compliance.py`. No `denial_text`, `patient_ref`, or free-text fields in `NotificationRecord`. |

---

## 13. Deliverables & Acceptance Criteria

### Slice Structure

G4 ships in two sub-slices on the `feature/g4-assignment-notifications` branch,
merged to `main` via PR:

| Sub-slice | Scope |
|---|---|
| **G4 Slice 1** — Assignment core | `AssignmentStore`, `AssignmentRecord`/`AssignmentEvent` models, three assignment routes, `GET /api/reviews/pending` extension, `AuditRecord.assignment_ref`, resume path integration, schema parity, unit + integration tests |
| **G4 Slice 2** — Notification system + UI | `NotificationStore`, `NotificationBus`, SLA ticker, notification routes, `GET /api/reviews/stream`, `hold` node hook, frontend `NotificationBell`, queue `assignee_id` display, capability manifest entries, UI unit tests |

### Acceptance Criteria

**G4 Slice 1:**
- [ ] `POST /api/cases/{id}/assign` self-claim returns `200 AssignmentRecord`; duplicate by different user returns `409`.
- [ ] `DELETE /api/cases/{id}/assign` by non-assignee reviewer returns `403`; by assignee returns `204`.
- [ ] `PATCH /api/cases/{id}/assign` by reviewer returns `403`; by supervisor returns `200`.
- [ ] `GET /api/reviews/pending` items include `assignee_id` and `assigned_at`.
- [ ] Full pipeline run → `POST /api/appeal/resume` (after assign) → `AuditRecord.assignment_ref == assignee_id`.
- [ ] Full pipeline run → `POST /api/appeal/resume` (no assign) → `AuditRecord.assignment_ref == null`.
- [ ] All G4-U-01–04 and G4-I-01–06 pass in CI.
- [ ] `test_schema_parity.py` updated and passes.
- [ ] Wire-types freshness gate passes (no stale generated types).
- [ ] `UserRole` enum in `schemas.py` and `src/types.ts` — identical members.
- [ ] `backend/.env.example` updated with `DEMO_SUPERVISOR_USER` / `DEMO_SUPERVISOR_PASSWORD`.

**G4 Slice 2:**
- [ ] Full exception-tier pipeline run: `NotificationStore` contains a `case_parked` record after `hold` fires (G4-I-11 passes).
- [ ] `GET /api/notifications` returns tenant-scoped records; Bearer caller sees all tenants.
- [ ] `POST /api/notifications/{id}/read` and `POST /api/notifications/read-all` work correctly.
- [ ] `GET /api/reviews/stream` delivers `notification` SSE event on `NotificationBus.publish()`; keepalive fires within 15 s.
- [ ] SLA ticker emits `sla_reminder` at 2 h and `sla_escalation` at 4 h; does not re-emit within the same poll interval (G4-U-11–13 pass).
- [ ] `NotificationBell` component renders unread count badge; badge increments on SSE event; "mark all read" clears badge (frontend unit tests pass).
- [ ] `ReviewQueue` shows `assignee_id` badge and SLA age indicator in live mode (frontend unit tests pass).
- [ ] All G4-U-05–14 and G4-I-07–11 pass in CI.
- [ ] PHI scan extension in `test_golden_compliance.py` covers notification `message` fields.
- [ ] `src/capabilities.ts` entries O14 and O15 added; `npm run build` passes.
- [ ] SLA threshold env vars documented in `backend/.env.example` and `06-api-contract.md`.
- [ ] This PRD document committed to `docs/prd/` in the same PR as G4 Slice 2.
